clue.text: Israeli leader needs a bit of time to take in account

indicators.note: the leader's name must take the bit of time inside itself, enclosing it

parts.note: Golda Meir, Prime Minister of Israel 1969-74
a mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: A busy Israeli prime minister needs a moment to absorb a financial statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' looks like a bank or bill account; it is the written narrative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A memoir is a personal written narrative of events, an account of the writer's life.

clue.text: Article about rescue service in old country

indicators.note: the article goes about, surrounding, the rescue service

parts.note: the definite article
the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British roadside breakdown rescue service

explanation.surface: A news article about an emergency service operating in some old country.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region and kingdom in the Balkans, now divided between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

clue.text: Preventing state can lead to good

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter, here of good

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Stopping some condition from arising might turn out for the best.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to ward it off, so averting means stopping it happening.

clue.text: I'd be no second ranker going after society

definitions.text: I'd be no second ranker going after society

indicators.note: the rest comes after the abbreviation for society

parts.note: taken as written
B is the second rank, as in B-list or grade B

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to be second-rate and chases after high society.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a portrait of the answer: a social climber who scorns anything second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on those of lower status and courts fashionable people, so would never accept second rank.

clue.text: Adult wanting acclaim? Get away!

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
to vaunt is to boast, showing off out of a desire for praise

explanation.surface: A grown-up craves applause and is told to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an archaic exclamation ordering someone to go away, as in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Old Indian getting about repeatedly — Delhi's original commander

parts.note: on means about, concerning, as in a talk on poetry
the word for about is given twice

indicators.note: the original of Delhi is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
an aga is an Ottoman military commander

explanation.surface: An Indian of long ago wanders around and around, with Delhi's founding general in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests India because of Delhi, but the answer is a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Onondaga are one of the Iroquois nations of North America, a people of the old Indian confederacy.

clue.text: Like Indian food taken after end of proceedings — rushed

indicators.note: the food word comes after the last letter, so it goes second
the end of proceedings is its last letter

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken
curried dishes are spiced in the Indian style

explanation.surface: A curry eaten once the meeting closed, before everyone dashed off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to move hurriedly with short quick steps, so scurried means hurried.

clue.text: Ice over one bath

parts.note: all fourteen letters are rearranged to give a composer, one letter short, and his named symphony

explanation.surface: A frozen layer forms across a single bathtub.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue with no definition or indicator: the whole clue rearranges to Beethoven, entered one E short, plus his Third Symphony. The clue itself lacks that E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eroica is the nickname of Beethoven's Third Symphony, so the composer and his work together are the answer.

clue.text: City can be very pleasant, English admitted

indicators.note: English is let in between the other pieces

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A city can be lovely indeed once the English are let in.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is itself a city, a tempting false lead; here it is just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the Italian city built on lagoon islands, famous for its canals.

clue.text: Shock about old books being rubbish?

definitions.note: an exclamation dismissing nonsense; the question mark marks the loose sense

indicators.note: the hair goes about, around, the old books

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Outrage that old volumes are being dismissed as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like surprise but is a mass of hair; OT is the Old Testament, the crossword's usual old books.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is empty, boastful talk, so the phrase means nonsense in the same way.

clue.text: Mark tub in corner)

parts.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged to give a composer, one letter short, and his named symphony

explanation.surface: Put a mark on the tub standing in the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue with no definition or indicator: the letters give Bruckner, entered without his C, plus the nickname of his Fourth Symphony. The stray bracket is in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruckner's Fourth Symphony is known as the Romantic, so the composer and his work together are the answer.

clue.text: See 20
Detests mitres perhaps, admitting eccentricity

indicators.note: the headwear lets the symbol in

parts.note: a mitre is a bishop's hat, an example of the class
e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic section

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes bishops' headgear yet admits a certain oddness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentricity' reads as oddness; in geometry it is written e.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to detest it, the two verbs being near synonyms for strong dislike.

clue.text: See 23
Then a goldfish darts around in deceptive movement

indicators.note: a goldfish darting around its bowl jumbles the letters into a new order

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A goldfish flitting about its bowl seems to perform a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is a conjuror's dexterous trick that deceives the eye with quick hand movements.

clue.text: City salvationists joined by member of religion possessing nothing

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
a Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism

explanation.surface: Salvation Army workers in a city team up with a believer who owns nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarasota is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida in the United States.

clue.text: Record exceptionally pithy eastern plant

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: taken unusually, the letters are rearranged out of their normal order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A record-breaking, unusually pithy plant from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphyte is a plant, such as an orchid, that grows on another plant without being a parasite.

clue.text: Mum, dad and the two kids perhaps running from 'ouse

definitions.text: Mum, dad and the two kids perhaps
definitions.note: a family of four is one example of the answer

indicators.note: the family running from the house sends these letters scattering

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters rearranged
house with its aitch dropped, Cockney style, giving four letters

explanation.surface: A family of four flee their house, dropped aitch and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ouse drops its H in Cockney style, leaving just the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A foursome is any group of four people, and a nuclear family of parents and two children is one.

clue.text: See 8
Powerful men always being hugged by a modern miss

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for always sits inside the arms of the other letters

parts.note: Ms is the modern title for a woman, married or not
e'er is the poetic short form of ever

explanation.surface: Strong men are forever being embraced by a young woman of today.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameers, or emirs, are Muslim rulers and commanders, men of power.

clue.text: He charms nun — sin!

parts.note: all fourteen letters are rearranged to give a composer, one letter short, and his named symphony

explanation.surface: A seducer woos a nun, and what a sin that is!
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue with no definition or indicator: the letters give Schumann, entered without his H, plus the nickname of his Third Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Schumann's Third Symphony is called the Rhenish, after the Rhine, so composer and work together are the answer.

clue.text: A smoker at home upset the old boys?

parts.note: taken as written
a lum is a chimney in Scots and northern English, something that smokes

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned over, read bottom to top

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A pipe-smoker at home has upset the elderly men of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' suggests a person; it is a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former pupils of a school or college, the British 'old boys'.

clue.text: Writer having cake served up is a bit of a lump

indicators.note: in a down clue the food is served upwards, so read from the bottom

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: An author eats a cake upside down and finds part of it lumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author; it is the tip of a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nubbin is a small knob or stub, a little lump or remnant of something.

clue.text: Bright cars etc

parts.note: all thirteen letters are rearranged to give a composer, one letter short, and his named symphony

explanation.surface: A list of gleaming, brightly coloured vehicles and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue with no definition or indicator: the letters give Schubert, entered without his U, plus the nickname of his Fourth Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert's Fourth Symphony is known as the Tragic, so the composer and his work together are the answer.

clue.text: Stuck in pot — a rotten plant

indicators.note: the answer is stuck inside the run of letters across these words

parts.note: the run of letters that holds the answer, read straight through

explanation.surface: A rotten specimen left wedged in its flowerpot.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a tropical plant grown for its starchy edible root, eaten as a staple.

clue.text: Son, overweight and squat

parts.note: tubby means plump, overweight

explanation.surface: A boy who is plump and short.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat as an adjective means short and thickset, and stubby means short and thick.

clue.text: Tell king from coin

parts.note: to state is to tell, declare

explanation.surface: A story of a king separated from his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' hints at William Tell, but it is just the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was an ancient Greek gold or silver coin.
